title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). I is a finite totally ordered set with least element ω0 and greatest element ω1, with ∂I = {ω0, ω1}. Grothendieck calls this a combinatorial oriented segment or 'pseudo-segment'. Its 'figures' or 'polygons' L are subobjects (presheaf-like subsystems) of I built from points a ∈ I (M_0) and elementary segments I_{a,b} (M_1). Each L has a complementary figure L*. For a vertex s, ord(s,L) is the number of segments of L incident to s. δL is the vertex set of L and ∂L its set of boundary vertices.

What this page does. It fixes the terminology and the canonical decomposition of δL needed for the duality L ↦ L*.
- Interior vertices s ∉ ∂I have ord ∈ {0,1,2}. A vertex with ord 2 is a 'proper interior' vertex.
- An endpoint s ∈ ∂I always has ord(s,L) ∈ {0,1}. This is checked on a single point {X} or a single segment, X ∈ M_1. An endpoint with ord 1 is adjoined as an 'improper interior' vertex.
- An interior vertex (proper or improper) is 'redundant' if it does not lie in δL*. Otherwise it is 'lacunary'.
- Ord-0 vertices are 'isolated'.

Identities under complementation:
- L*_is = L_lac and L*_lac = L_is, so isolated and lacunary vertices swap.
- L_red = δL − δL*.
- δL = (L_red ∪ L_lac ∪ L_is) ∪ ∂L. The first three terms form L_int.
- ∂L = ∂_0 L ⊔ ∂'_0 L. Here ∂_0 L = L_0 ∩ ∂L are the boundary vertices, and ∂'_0 L are the improper vertices.

Grothendieck then looks for a truly disjoint decomposition δL = L_red ∪ L_is ∪ L_lac ∪ ∂*L, with ∂*L = ∂L minus (∂L_0 ∩ ∂I), the non-extremal boundary vertices. The only overlap left is ∂L ∩ L_int: the points of ∂I that are vertices of L but not isolated points of L.

The next page completes this into a 'canonical decomposition'. In it the lacunary and isolated parts are exchanged by duality, ∂*L is invariant, and the redundant part disappears under duality, with part of it reappearing under bidualité. It also introduces 'evanescent' and 'semi-evanescent' vertices.

Purpose. This is careful combinatorial bookkeeping for a complementation duality on subcomplexes of a subdivided oriented 1-simplex. It is presumably a building block for the 'Ateliers' chapter on combinatorial (simplicial/ordered) models of segments.
errors: No genuine mathematical errors are visible. The text is a working draft: Grothendieck rewrites the definitions of improper interior vertices and corrects the disjointness claims (e.g. the overlap ∂L ∩ L_int = ∂I ∩ (L_0 ∖ L_is)).

The first decomposition δL = L_red ∪ L_lac ∪ L_is ∪ ∂L is not disjoint, as Grothendieck himself notes. The candidate disjoint version still overlaps at endpoints in ∂I, which is why the next page revises it.

ideas.what: Classification of vertices of a sub-figure of a combinatorial oriented segment by incidence order (isolated / boundary / proper or improper interior), with redundant vs. lacunary distinguished by membership in the complementary figure.
ideas.modern_name: Vertex degree classification in a subgraph of a path graph; complementation/Alexander-type duality for subcomplexes of a subdivided interval

ideas.what: Duality L ↦ L* exchanging isolated and lacunary vertices, with the redundant vertices being exactly δL − δL*.
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial complement duality on a 1-dimensional ordered complex

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary terminological bookkeeping for a complement duality of figures in a finite ordered segment. It is careful but routine, and there is no substantial result or connection beyond what is folklore.
transcription_corrections: The '14' at the top is Grothendieck's own page number; '17' at the bottom is the archive page number.
'me sont par clairs' probably reads 'me semblent clairs' or 'me sont clairs'.
'il faut joindre' is more likely 'il faut adjoindre'.
'à l'exclusion de 2/2[?]' is probably 'à l'exclusion de 2', i.e. ord ≠ 2 for s ∈ ∂I.
'pour Ar L' is uncertain; it may be 'pour tout L' or 'card L'. 'sur les lts de ∂I' is likely 'sur les pts (points) de ∂I'.
'sont mieux disjoints' probably reads 'sont mutuellement disjoints'.
In the last sentence, 'les points de δL qui sont intérieurs sont ceux qui sont dans ∂I sans être des points isolés de L' refers to the overlap ∂L ∩ L_int, consistent with ∂I ∩ (L_0 ∖ L_is).
